attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6 found that the R5.1 receipt's `source_registry.records` said 7 over a 9-record file — and the same receipt's digest list PINS that 9-record file and matches its bytes, so it asserted two things about one file and the gate checked the wrong one. Generalising the check found the failure was worse one file over. Three hand-typed counts in CLAIM_LEDGER.json said 51 where the ledger held 61 settled claims (at INV-R5.2), and one gave the witness ratio as 47 of 51 where the gate computed 45 of 49 (at INV-R5.2). (Writing this record tripped the new check twice, because quoting a stale number reads exactly like asserting one — which is why the convention is that a historical count names its round.) Two of the four sat inside the `evidence` fields of MOS-CLAIM-OBLIGATION and MOS-OBJECTIVE-MEASUREMENT — the records asserting the obligation and measurement invariants they had drifted from, which is the least likely place a reader looks. H5 said no count a checker can compute is typed by hand; it was enforced on the review bundle's placeholders and on the published law totals, and nowhere on the canonical data. §6 now walks every {file, records} pair in the receipt and §7 scans the ledger's own prose. A number about a past round is legal and must say so: `61 settled claims (at INV-R5)`.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5.1 audit §4. H5-COUNTS-ARE-DERIVED, paid for by INV-R4.1.
